checks.expected: a pure helper (one data arg, no effects) and register_user(data, database, mailer) exist

checks.name: validation-independent-of-effects
checks.expected: _normalize_and_validate has no persistence, mail, time, filesystem, or output effects

checks.name: entry-point-orchestrates-boundaries
checks.expected: register_user uses _normalize_and_validate, then persists and sends welcome email

checks.name: direct-helper-tests
checks.expected: at least two distinct test functions directly call _normalize_and_validate
checks.actual: test_empty_name_raises, test_invalid_email_ends_with_at_raises, test_invalid_email_missing_at_raises, test_invalid_email_starts_with_at_raises, test_missing_name_raises, test_normalizes_name_and_email, test_whitespace_only_email_raises
checks.evidence: AST inspection of test_* function bodies for direct Call(Name('_normalize_and_validate'))

checks.name: no-mock-heavy-test-setup
checks.expected: use lightweight fakes rather than mocks

command:
Refactor registration.py so input normalization and registration validation can be tested without a database or email sender. Keep the public `register_user(data, database, mailer)` function and its current behavior. Extract a pure helper that handles input normalization and validation, keeping persistence and the welcome message in `register_user`.

Add tests covering normalized input and invalid email/name cases. Keep the existing lightweight fake-based integration tests. Do not add interfaces, classes, mocks, network dependencies, or test-only public APIs. Run the tests and keep the change scoped to `registration.py` and `tests/test_registration.py`.
